chunks: Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, that he said:

Regarding khulʿ: if she says to him, 'I will not perform ghusl for you from janabah, nor will I fulfill an oath for you, and I will surely let into your bed one whom you dislike,' then when she says this to him, it becomes permissible for him to divorce her by khulʿ, and it becomes lawful for him what he has taken from her.

key_terms.أَخَذَ مِنْهَا: what he took from her; the compensation given in khulʿ
key_terms.أَغْتَسِلُ: I perform ghusl; here referring to ritual bathing after janabah
key_terms.أُبِرُّ: I fulfill or honor; here in relation to a sworn oath or obligation
key_terms.الْخُلْعِ: khulʿ; a form of divorce involving separation with compensation from the wife
key_terms.جَنَابَةٍ: janabah; the state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.فِرَاشَكَ: your bed; referring to the marital bed
key_terms.يَخْلَعَهَا: that he may separate from her by khulʿ

ai.seo_question: When is khulʿ permissible, and is the compensation taken from the wife lawful?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning khulʿ, a form of separation initiated in the context of severe marital discord. It states that when the wife openly declares conduct showing breakdown of conjugal commitment, khulʿ becomes permissible and the compensation taken from her is lawful.
